name: ReviewPine: Google Reviews Widget, Slider and Badge
author: ainygotechnologies

sections.description:
ReviewPine is a Google reviews widget for WordPress. Embed your real Google reviews on any page as a reviews slider, grid, list, badge or floating widget, in a design that fits your brand. Find your business by name, pick a layout and paste one shortcode. New Google reviews show up by themselves.

Let your happiest customers do the talking, right where visitors decide to buy, book or get in touch.

Start with a free trial. Try every layout and the full customiser free during your trial. After it, one widget can stay live on the Free plan with your 10 newest 4 and 5 star reviews.

What you get

  • 21 layouts for every spot: slider, two-way slider, grid, list, sidebar and spotlight; bento wall, card stack and rating showcase; Trust, Google and rating badges, a rating line and pill; and edge-of-page widgets: floating badge, review toasts, side tab, review bubble, corner card and phone review bar.
  • Light and dark, your colours: every layout comes in light and dark, with 24 ready-made looks, your own colours, fonts, headline and text, and a live preview.
  • Always up to date: new Google reviews appear on your site automatically. Nothing to copy or paste again.
  • Show it on every page with one click: edge-of-page widgets need no shortcode.
  • Review us on Google button: invite happy customers to leave a review.
  • Fast pages: about 28 KB, loaded after your page, no layout shift; the plugin adds nothing to pages without a widget.
  • No view limits: no counting of page views, on any plan.
  • Privacy friendly: the widget sets no cookies, uses no browser storage and does no tracking, so it adds nothing to your cookie banner.
  • Mobile friendly and accessible: layouts adapt to any screen and work with a keyboard and screen readers.
  • Works with your setup: the block editor, page builders, widget areas and caching plugins.
  • For agencies: manage every client’s business from one account. Yearly plans cover 1, 5 or 25 businesses, with invoices (GST invoices in India).
  • For web designers and freelancers: resell ReviewPine to your clients at volume prices, or refer them and earn 25% of their first year. See the partner programme: https://reviewpine.com/partners

How it works

  1. Create a free ReviewPine account, add your business (search it by name, or paste its Google Maps link) and pick a widget design.
  2. In WordPress, open ReviewPine and click Connect ReviewPine.
  3. Click Copy shortcode on a widget and paste it into any page, post or widget area.

Design changes you make later on ReviewPine show on your site by themselves.

Good to know

  • A ReviewPine account is needed. ReviewPine is an online service by Ainygo Technologies that fetches your business’s public Google reviews (see External services below). Creating an account is free and starts with a free trial.
  • Safe by design. Connecting gives this site read-only access to your widget list (names and shortcodes). It can’t change anything in your ReviewPine account, and you can disconnect at any time.
  • Free plan. After the free trial, one widget can stay live for free with your 10 newest 4 and 5 star reviews. Free widgets show a small “Free widget by ReviewPine” link above the reviews. Paid plans remove the link and show your recent reviews, up to several hundred per business.

External services

This plugin relies on ReviewPine, an external service provided by Ainygo Technologies (https://reviewpine.com). ReviewPine fetches a business’s public Google reviews and displays them in a widget. The plugin needs it to list your widgets in wp-admin and to show the widgets on your pages. You need a ReviewPine account, and nothing is sent to ReviewPine until you click Connect.

The plugin uses two ReviewPine addresses:

1. ReviewPine app: https://app.reviewpine.com (wp-admin only)

  • When you click Connect, your browser opens https://app.reviewpine.com/connect/wordpress, where you sign in and approve the connection. Sent: your site’s address, the address of the plugin’s admin page and a one-time security value.
  • Right after you approve, WordPress sends https://app.reviewpine.com/api/wp/v1/token the one-time code, a verification value and your site’s address, and receives a read-only connection token plus your ReviewPine account name and a masked email address.
  • When the plugin page is opened (at most once every 12 hours) or you click Refresh list, WordPress requests https://app.reviewpine.com/api/wp/v1/widgets. Sent: the connection token and your site’s address. Received: your widget names, business names, layouts and statuses.
  • When you click Disconnect or delete the plugin, WordPress sends the connection token to https://app.reviewpine.com/api/wp/v1/disconnect so ReviewPine deletes the connection.

2. ReviewPine widget: https://cdn.reviewpine.com (public pages and the preview)

  • On pages that contain the [reviewpine] shortcode, each visitor’s browser loads the widget script https://cdn.reviewpine.com/widget.v1.js and then the widget’s reviews (https://cdn.reviewpine.com/w/WIDGET-ID.json) when the visitor scrolls near the widget. If you choose Show on every page for a floating badge, every page of your site loads the same script and that widget’s reviews after the page has loaded. Like any file request, this involves the visitor’s IP address and browser details. The widget sets no cookies, uses no browser storage and sends no tracking or analytics data. Reviewer profile pictures and the Google logo shown in the widget are loaded from Google’s servers.
  • When you click Preview on the plugin page in wp-admin, your browser loads the same widget script and reviews from https://cdn.reviewpine.com to show the widget.

ReviewPine terms of service: https://reviewpine.com/terms
ReviewPine privacy policy: https://reviewpine.com/privacy
Google privacy policy (profile pictures and logo): https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open ReviewPine in the admin menu and click Connect ReviewPine.
  3. Click Copy shortcode on a widget and paste it where the reviews should appear.
sections.faq:
How do I add Google reviews to my WordPress site?

Install ReviewPine, click Connect ReviewPine, find your business by name on ReviewPine and pick a layout, then paste the widget’s shortcode into a page. No Google API key, no Google login and no code.

Can I show Google reviews as a slider, carousel or badge?

Yes. Choose from 21 layouts: sliders (carousels), grids, lists, a spotlight, a bento wall, Google and rating badges, a floating badge, review toasts, a side tab and more. Every layout comes in light and dark.

Do I need a ReviewPine account?

Yes. Creating one is free and starts with a free trial. Click Create free account on the plugin page.

Where do I design my widget?

On ReviewPine. Click Create or edit widgets on the plugin page: ReviewPine opens in a new tab, and when you come back, Refresh widget list loads your new widgets. Design changes appear on your site automatically.

I made a new widget but don’t see it

Click Refresh list on the plugin page.

What happens if I disconnect?

Every ReviewPine widget stops showing on this site: all their shortcodes show nothing, and a floating badge set for every page is hidden. If your site uses a caching plugin we can’t clear automatically, clear its cache once so visitors see the change. Nothing is deleted. Connect again and they show again. If the connection is removed from your ReviewPine account instead (Your account → Connected sites), widgets already on your pages keep showing until you remove their shortcodes.

Does the plugin add links or credits to my website?

The plugin’s own code adds no links or credits. It adds only an empty container and the ReviewPine widget script where you place the shortcode. The widget itself is produced by the ReviewPine service: it shows your reviews with the required Google attribution, and widgets on ReviewPine’s Free plan also show a small “Free widget by ReviewPine” link. Paid plans remove that link. Nothing is added to pages without the shortcode, unless you choose Show on every page for a floating badge.

How do I show a floating badge on every page?

Choose the Floating badge layout for a widget on ReviewPine, click Refresh list on the plugin page, then Turn on next to Show on every page on that widget. Click Turn off to remove it. You can also paste its shortcode on chosen pages only.

What does Preview do?

It shows your widget in a popup exactly as visitors see it. The preview runs in a sandboxed frame that loads only the ReviewPine widget script and your reviews from cdn.reviewpine.com. It is isolated from wp-admin, so it cannot read or change anything in your dashboard, and nothing loads until you click Preview.

Does it work with caching and optimisation plugins?

Yes. Pages with the shortcode can be fully cached: the reviews are not stored in the page but loaded by the visitor’s browser, so cached pages still show your latest reviews and you never need to clear the cache when reviews change. The widget script carries the standard opt-out markers for Cloudflare Rocket Loader, LiteSpeed Cache and WP Rocket, so those tools leave it as it is. If another optimisation plugin combines or delays external scripts and the reviews don’t appear, exclude widget.v1.js in its settings.

Do I need to mention it in my privacy policy?

The plugin suggests text for your privacy policy under Settings → Privacy → Policy Guide, explaining what visitors’ browsers load from ReviewPine and Google. The widget sets no cookies, so it adds nothing to your cookie banner.
sections.changelog:
1.0.14

  • When ReviewPine disconnects the site, the plugin page says so at once (it used to show only after the next visit).
  • A suspended ReviewPine account now gets its own clear message instead of “could not be reached”.
  • The plugin acts on a “disconnected” or “suspended” answer only when ReviewPine itself gives it; any other refusal (for example from a firewall in between) shows the last saved list, as when ReviewPine can’t be reached.
  • While ReviewPine can’t be reached, the plugin page keeps showing your last saved widget list (it used to show “No widgets yet” after a few minutes).
  • Widgets keep their space on the page while they load, also after the 12-hour list cache ends: the plugin remembers each widget’s layout.
  • Clearer description of the free trial and the Free plan.

1.0.13

  • Uninstalling also removes the plugin’s short-lived connection data.
  • Wording: “4 and 5 star reviews”, and the plugin’s current name in the privacy policy text.

1.0.12

  • Clearer plugin name and description: embed Google reviews as a slider, grid, badge or floating widget.
  • Two new questions in the FAQ, and a line for web designers about the partner programme.
  • The plugin page has two quiet links under the guide: rate the plugin on WordPress.org, and the ReviewPine partner programme for people who build sites for clients.

1.0.11

  • The ReviewPine logo’s top colour is now blue (#1A73E8) in the plugin icon, banners, screenshots and admin pages.

1.0.10

  • Plugin description updated: all 21 layouts, light and dark looks, the free plan, no view limits. No code changes.

1.0.9

  • The new ReviewPine layouts show with their own names on the plugin page: Spotlight, Bento wall, Card stack, Rating showcase, Review toasts, Side tab, Review bubble, Corner card and Phone review bar.
  • Show on every page now works for every widget that sits at the edge of the page (floating badge, review toasts, side tab, review bubble, corner card, phone review bar), not only the floating badge.

1.0.8

  • Disconnecting now hides every ReviewPine widget on this site (all shortcodes and the floating badge) until you connect again, after a short confirmation.
  • Disconnecting, connecting again and turning the every-page badge on or off clear the page cache of popular caching plugins (LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache, SiteGround, Hummingbird, Breeze, Cache Enabler), so visitors see the change right away.
  • A floating badge set for every page can be turned off from the plugin page even while the site is not connected.

1.0.7

  • Floating badge on every page: one click on the plugin page shows a floating badge widget across your site, no shortcode needed.
  • Redesigned plugin page: clearer widget cards with the full shortcode, a Copy shortcode button and a short guide to adding a widget to a page.
  • Create or edit widgets: a short guide opens ReviewPine in a new tab, then offers Refresh widget list when you come back.

1.0.6

  • The return from the ReviewPine connection screen is now verified with a WordPress nonce.
  • ReviewPine service addresses are fixed in the code and documented in full under External services.
  • Clearer two-step setup screen: create your free account first, then connect.
  • The connection return is handled only on the plugin’s own page.
  • Works out of the box with Cloudflare Rocket Loader, LiteSpeed Cache and WP Rocket.
  • Suggested privacy policy text under Settings → Privacy.

1.0.3

  • Embed scripts are now loaded through WordPress’s script system.
  • The setup reminder appears only on the Plugins screen and can be dismissed for good.

1.0.2

  • Security hardening: widget scripts and links accepted only from reviewpine.com, safer network calls, faster admin when ReviewPine can’t be reached, clean multisite uninstall.

1.0.1

  • Preview opens in a popup with Desktop, Tablet and Mobile sizes.

1.0.0

  • First release: connect your account, list widgets, copy shortcodes, preview.
